NEW YORK — In a press conference Thursday morning that began with routine remarks about tourism and ended in visible confusion, Mayor Mamdani announced that

Times Square will soon be officially renamed “New Red Square,” a move he repeatedly emphasized has “absolutely nothing to do with communism.”

“I just like red,” the mayor said, standing before a backdrop that had, for the occasion, been subtly adjusted to a deeper shade. “It’s a strong color. It’s bold. It’s energetic. New York is energetic. This is not complicated.”
articles.body:
**NEW YORK — In a press conference Thursday morning that began with routine remarks about tourism and ended in visible confusion, Mayor Mamdani announced that**

**Times Square will soon be officially renamed “New Red Square,” a move he repeatedly emphasized has “absolutely nothing to do with communism.”**

**“I just like red,” the mayor said, standing before a backdrop that had, for the occasion, been subtly adjusted to a deeper shade. “It’s a strong color. It’s bold. It’s energetic. New York is energetic. This is not complicated.”**

**The plan, which will take effect later this summer pending what aides described as “minimal logistical adjustments,” includes updated signage, rebranding efforts, and a coordinated push to “lean into red as a unifying visual theme.”**

**City officials stressed that the name change is purely aesthetic.**

**“People hear ‘Red Square’ and they jump to conclusions,” said one senior advisor. “This is about branding. This is about vibrancy. This is about a mayor who, frankly, prefers one color over others.”**

**Still, the announcement has prompted questions.**

**When asked directly whether the name carried any historical or ideological connotations, the mayor shook his head.**

**“No,” he said. “None. I have never been to the other one. I don’t think about the other one. This is a completely separate red square.”**

**Tourism officials appeared cautiously**

**optimistic, noting that Times Square has long thrived on spectacle and reinvention.**

**“If people want to come take photos in a place called New Red Square, they will,” said one representative. “They already come here to stand in the middle of traffic and look up.”**

**The rebranding effort is expected to include a shift in lighting design, with several major billboards reportedly agreeing to incorporate more red tones during peak hours. Early mockups depict the square bathed in a uniform crimson glow, which one planner described as “striking, possibly overwhelming, but definitely consistent.”**

**Local reaction has been mixed.**

**“I mean, it’s already a lot,” said one visitor from Ohio, glancing around the square. “I’m not sure making it redder is the issue we’re facing.”**

**Others expressed support, if only for the clarity.**

**“At least now it sounds like what it feels like,” said a street performer dressed as Spider-Man. “A little intense. A little aggressive. Kind of hard to leave.”**

**Back at City Hall, the mayor acknowledged that some residents might take time to adjust.**

**“Change is part of what makes New York great,” he said. “Also, again, it’s just a color.” He paused briefly before adding, “And it’s a very good one."**
articles.deck: Mayor Announces Plan to Rename Times Square ‘New Red Square,’ Insists It’s Just a Color Preference
articles.author: Mort Adella
articles.title: Mayor Announces Plan to Rename Times Square “New Red Square”, Insists it’s Just a Color Preference

Participants—men and women alike—will compete in a series of timed pelvic floor endurance rounds, during which they must contract and release targeted muscle groups while maintaining uninterrupted eye contact with an opposing competitor.

articles.body:
**NEW YORK, NY — In what is being hailed as one of the most unusual athletic competitions in recent memory, Kegel USA will take place this Thursday at the historic Armory in Manhattan.**


**Organizers expect nearly 200 competitors from across the country to gather in pursuit of a single title: *King (or Queen) of Kegels.***

![](kegel-trophy.jpg)

**Participants—men and women alike—will compete in a series of timed pelvic floor endurance rounds, during which they must contract and release targeted muscle groups while maintaining uninterrupted eye contact with an opposing competitor.**


**“It’s about control, focus, and composure under pressure,” one event coordinator said. “People underestimate how quickly things can unravel.”**


**Indeed, early observers describe the competition as less a test of strength and more a battle of psychological endurance.**


**“It’s intense,” said one returning competitor. “The eye contact alone can break you.”**


**Medical personnel will be on-site, as organizers acknowledge that vagal responses—including lightheadedness and near-fainting—are not uncommon. Loss of eye contact, however, remains the most frequent cause of disqualification.**

![](kegel-injury.jpg)

**“There’s a moment where you realize you’re either locked in… or you’re out,” said a judge familiar with the scoring process.**


**Despite skepticism from parts of the medical community, proponents argue that the event represents the next frontier in competitive fitness.**

**“There’s been CrossFit, there’s been ultramarathons,” one attendee noted. “This is just… different.”**


**Doors open at 6 p.m., with preliminary rounds beginning shortly thereafter. Finals are expected to draw a standing-room-only crowd.**


**As for what spectators should expect?**


**“Silence,” one organizer said. “A lot of silence… and eye contact and very little urination.**
articles.deck: Organizers expect nearly 200 competitors from across the country to gather in pursuit of a single title: King (or Queen) of Kegels.
articles.author: Margaux Tilden
articles.title: Kegel USA” Set to Take Over NYC Armory in One of the Strangest Competitions on Record

articles.body:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Following his return from a high-profile visit to China, former President Donald Trump dismissed the trip as “not a big deal,” describing it instead as a casual excursion and an opportunity to bring along several top American CEOs for what he called “a short holiday.”


“We had a good time,” Trump told reporters. “People are making it into something much bigger than it was. It wasn’t meant to be a big deal—it was more of an excursion. A little trip.” According to Trump, the visit—initially framed by some observers as diplomatically significant—was, in reality, more informal in nature. “I said, why not bring some of our great business leaders?” he added. “These are the top CEOs, the best. They work hard. They deserve a little break too.” Sources familiar with the trip described a loosely structured itinerary that included meetings, sightseeing, and what one attendee called “extended conversations about deals that may or may not exist.”


While details remain unclear, Trump emphasized that no major agreements were expected going into the visit.

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-2.08.08 am.png "Trump and Xi enjoy some paddling together")

“There was no pressure,” he said. “We weren’t signing anything big. If something happened, great. If not, we had a nice time.” Critics, however, questioned the framing of the trip, noting the unusual combination of high-level executives and the lack of a clearly defined diplomatic objective. “This is not typically how international engagement is described,” one analyst noted.


Still, attendees appeared to embrace the tone. “It had a very relaxed feel,” said one CEO who requested anonymity. “Part business, part… something else.” When asked whether future trips might follow a similar format, Trump did not rule it out.  “We’ll see,” he said. “People like trips.”
articles.deck: Trump Downplays China Trip, Calls It “Basically a Short Holiday With CEOs”
articles.author: The Public Record
articles.title: Trump Downplays China Trip, Calls It “Basically a Short Holiday With CEOs”

From stitched-together infant garments to shaved heads and exaggerated softness rituals, a new internet-born trend asks an uncomfortable question: What if growing up itself became unfashionable?

By So Cialdisease

Every generation develops a visual language for rebellion. Punk tore holes in convention. Grunge romanticized neglect. The internet era perfected optimization—skin care, fitness, self-branding, productivity and “looksmaxxing.”

But a growing online movement known as “BabyMaxxing” appears to reject not merely adulthood, but the entire concept of maturity itself.
articles.body:
*From stitched-together infant garments to shaved heads and exaggerated softness rituals, a new internet-born trend asks an uncomfortable question: What if growing up itself became unfashionable?*

By So Cialdisease

Every generation develops a visual language for rebellion. Punk tore holes in convention. Grunge romanticized neglect. The internet era perfected optimization—skin care, fitness, self-branding, productivity and “looksmaxxing.”

But a growing online movement known as “BabyMaxxing” appears to reject not merely adulthood, but the entire concept of maturity itself.

Across TikTok, Discord servers, and highly curated Instagram accounts, teenagers and young adults are assembling elaborate outfits from repurposed infant clothing: pastel onesies transformed into patchwork jackets, bib fabrics sewn into oversized collars, and tiny cartoon prints stitched together into uncanny runway silhouettes. The result resembles less a nostalgic throwback than what one fashion critic called “a surrealist infant collage.”

> *“It’s deeply unsettling,” said fashion historian Lena Vireaux. “But also strangely coherent as social commentary.”*

BabyMaxxing began, according to internet researchers, as a parody of “looksmaxxing” culture—the sprawling online ecosystem devoted to maximizing attractiveness through obsessive self-improvement. But as with many digital subcultures, irony quickly hardened into identity.

Participants document extensive “softness routines” online: shaving their heads to achieve what some describe as a “newborn silhouette,” pursuing elaborate skin and foot treatments intended to create “untouched texture,” and redesigning living spaces in muted nursery palettes.

Some adherents reportedly adopt exaggeratedly childlike mannerisms in public spaces, speaking in simplified tones or dramatizing ordinary movements with performative awkwardness. Videos tagged #BabyMaxxing frequently feature young adults waddling through grocery stores in oversized pastel clothing while ambient lullaby music plays over slowed footage.

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-2.11.35 am.png "Dr. Cole provides support to parents of Babymaxxers")

> *“It’s not about literally wanting to become infants,” said Dr. Marissa Cole, a psychologist at NYU who studies internet identity formation. “It’s about escaping performance pressure. These are young people raised in a world where every aspect of existence feels optimized, monetized, ranked, or judged. BabyMaxxing romanticizes a state where someone else cared for you completely.”*

Several school districts have reportedly issued guidance to counselors after students began incorporating increasingly immersive roleplay elements into daily life. Some parents describe the movement as less a fashion trend than “collective regression theater.”

Online, however, participants insist outsiders are misunderstanding the aesthetic.

One viral post reads: “Previous generations wanted independence. We want supervised nap time.”

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-2.11.41 am.png "Babymaxxing at a local Target")

Luxury brands are already circling the phenomenon. At Copenhagen Fashion Week, one avant-garde label unveiled a collection featuring oversized quilted silhouettes, bonnet-inspired headpieces and shoes designed to resemble enlarged toddler footwear. Critics described the show as “terrifying,” “brilliant,” and “emotionally exhausting.”

Whether BabyMaxxing survives beyond its current algorithmic moment remains unclear. Internet aesthetics often burn brightly and disappear within months.

Still, cultural observers argue the movement reveals something deeper than simple weirdness.

> *“In every era,” Vireaux said, “fashion reflects the anxieties people can’t articulate directly. And right now, many young people seem profoundly exhausted by the expectations attached to adulthood itself.”*

**“What if the real luxury was never having to grow up?”**

Perhaps that is why the movement’s unofficial slogan—circulating widely beneath outfit photos and nursery-themed mood boards—feels less like a joke than a generational confession: “What if the real luxury was never having to grow up?”
articles.deck: Babymaxxer’s roam the halls at a local school
articles.author: The Public Record
articles.title: Inside “BabyMaxxing,” Fashion’s Most Unsettling New Youth Aesthetic

The claims surfaced during a sprawling three- hour episode of The Joe Rogan Experience, where Rogan, mid-conversation about ancestral diets and modern health optimization, pivoted into what he called “the next frontier.”
articles.body:
**AUSTIN, TX — In a moment that left even longtime listeners blinking in disbelief, podcast host Joe Rogan stunned his audience this week with what he described as “compelling emerging evidence” that adult men who continue to consume human breast milk experience a cascade of benefits — including higher testosterone levels, expanded perineal dimensions, and dramatically increased lifespan.**

**The claims surfaced during a sprawling three- hour episode of *The Joe Rogan Experience*, where Rogan, mid-conversation about ancestral diets and modern health optimization, pivoted into what he called “the next frontier.”**

**“People are sleeping on this,” Rogan said, leaning forward. “We’ve been talking about cold plunges, elk meat, sauna protocols — but nobody’s talking about the original human fuel.”**

**Listeners initially assumed it was a bit. It was not. Rogan went on to reveal that he and longtime producer Jamie Vernon have quietly employed a full-time wet nurse as part of their daily regimen. According to Rogan, the practice has become as routine as his morning workout.**

**“Look, I’m already doing stem cells, ivermectin protocols, heat shock proteins in the sauna,” he explained. “This is just another layer. About 18 ounces a day. Clean, fresh, straight from the source. You wash that down with elk — you feel different.”**

**While Rogan did not cite specific peer- reviewed studies, he referenced “guys in certain circles” and “some wild data coming out of Eastern Europe” suggesting correlations between breast milk consumption and what he described as “structural expansion in the perineal zone.”**

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-2.16.34 am.png "Graph depicting Rogan’s new data set")

**When pressed by a guest on what that meant, Rogan clarified: “Taint width. Diameter. It’s measurable. It’s real.”**

**The internet responded swiftly, with reactions ranging from fascination to outright confusion. Clips of the segment racked up millions of views within hours, spawning hashtags like #MilkMaxxing and #TaintScience.**

**Adding fuel to the fire, presidential candidate Robert F. Kennedy Jr. reportedly acknowledged the trend during a campaign stop the following day, suggesting that current dietary guidelines may be “missing a foundational element.”**

**“We’ve ignored traditional human nourishment systems for too long,” Kennedy said. “If we’re serious about health, we need to revisit the pyramid — from the ground up.”**

**According to sources close to the campaign, Kennedy is informally exploring a proposal dubbed “Breast Force,” a federally supported initiative aimed at increasing access to human breast milk through a network of compensated providers. Funding, aides say, could be redirected from existing international aid budgets.**

**The proposal has not yet been formally introduced, though early internal drafts reportedly describe it as “a cornerstone of the MAHA movement’s nutritional sovereignty platform.” Public health experts, meanwhile, have urged caution.**

**“This is not a recognized or evidence-based practice for adult health,” said one nutrition researcher who asked not to be named. “And the specific claims being made are... unconventional.”**

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-2.16.42 am.png "MAHA gets behind breastmilk initiative")

**Back in Austin, Rogan appeared unfazed by the backlash. “People laughed at saunas. People laughed at ice baths,” he said toward the end of the episode. “You gotta be open. The truth is weird sometimes.”**

**As of press time, several supplement companies had already announced plans to release “lab-derived analogs,” while at least one startup teased a subscription-based delivery service promising “farm-to-table human nutrition.”**

**Whether this marks the beginning of a new wellness frontier or simply another strange chapter in the ever-expanding universe of biohacking remains to be seen. For now, one thing is clear:**

**The discourse has... expanded**
articles.deck: On his podcast Rogan consumes breast milk
articles.author: The Public Record
articles.title: Joe Rogan’s Latest Health Hack? 18 Ounces of Breastmilk a Day!

BEIJING — In what aides are describing as “a bold fusion of diplomacy and aesthetics,” former President Donald Trump arrived in Beijing this week accompanied not by trade officials or military advisors, but by a little-known internet personality named Clavicular—introduced to Chinese leadership as “a tremendous guy, incredible bone structure, maybe the best clavicles anyone’s ever seen.”

The visit, which officials insist is part of a broader effort to secure access to rare earth minerals, quickly veered into unfamiliar territory as Trump reportedly pivoted from tariffs and supply chains to what he repeatedly called “looksmaxxing.”

“China wants to look good, we all want to look good,” Trump said during a press availability on Air Force One. “And nobody understands structure better than this guy. Look at that—unbelievable. Strong, but elegant. We’re bringing that to China.”

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-2.21.54 am.png "Clavicular holding an inservice on facial remodeling with Chinese Troops")

Clavicular, whose online presence is devoted largely to analyzing facial symmetry, posture, and what he calls “upper-torso geometry,” was given an unexpected platform during closed-door sessions, where sources say he delivered a presentation titled *‘Maximizing National Aesthetic Output: A Strategic Framework.’*

According to one official briefed on the meeting, the pitch included recommendations ranging from posture initiatives to “national collarbone awareness campaigns,” though it remains unclear how these proposals relate to mineral extraction or trade policy.

Chinese officials appeared measured in their response. A spokesperson for the Ministry of Commerce described the talks as “wide-ranging” and “occasionally confusing,” but did not rule out continued dialogue.

“There was discussion of minerals,” the spokesperson said carefully. “There was also discussion of... alignment.”

Back in Washington, reactions have been mixed. Supporters praised the move as unconventional but effective.

Clavicular holding a seminar on facial remodeling

“He’s thinking outside the box,” said one longtime ally. “Other presidents bring economists. He brings visionaries. That’s why he wins.”

Critics, however, questioned whether the administration’s approach reflects a coherent strategy or something closer to performance art.

“This is what happens when diplomacy becomes vibes- based,” said one foreign policy analyst. “We appear to be negotiating critical supply chains using the language of a fitness subreddit.”

Despite the confusion, Trump remained optimistic as he departed Beijing, telling reporters that progress had been made.

“They loved it,” he said. “They loved Clavicular. We’re going to have the best-looking trade deal you’ve ever seen.”

At press time, no formal agreement on rare earth minerals had been announced, though sources confirm that several senior officials were observed standing noticeably straighter

articles.body:
**LOS ANGELES** — In a move that has left city officials, cultural critics, and much of the public stunned, a new theme park with alleged ties to Mexico’s Sinaloa cartel has quietly opened on the outskirts of Los Angeles—billing itself as an “immersive cultural experience” aimed at “reframing perception through entertainment.” The park, known as“NarcoLand: The Experience,” presents a surreal blend of amusement park spectacle and dark satire, attempting—according to its promotional materials—to

“highlight misunderstood narratives” while offering guests a highly unconventional day out.

Whether it succeeds in that mission remains fiercely debated. Visitors entering the park are greeted by actors portraying sharply dressed “security personnel,” who—true to the park’s controversial concept— openly accept bribes as part of the experience. Guests can exchange cash for expedited ride access, backstage entry, or simply the novelty of “bending the rules.” Inside, the attractions lean heavily into shock value.

One of the most talked-about rides, “El Baño Final,” uses motion simulation, heat effects, and immersive audio to recreate what the park describes as a high-intensity escape scenario. Riders are placed in a chamber designed to simulate a slow descent into a vat of acid—though organizers insist it is purely theatrical. For younger visitors, the park offers activities that have drawn equal parts fascination and outrage.

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-2.26.26 am.png)

Children can receive temporary face tattoos styled after cartel iconography and participate in interactive games that critics say blur the line between play and deeply troubling themes.

Perhaps the most controversial attraction is a VR experience titled “Crossing Lines.” Guests engage in a simulated hostage scenario involving a school bus. The park defends the exhibit as a psychological exploration ofdecision-making under pressure.

At the center of the park stands “The Hall of Influence,” a parody of Disney’s Hall of Presidents. Animatronic figures resembling political leaders deliver scripted monologues before engaging in dramatized negotiations involving bribes and trafficking.

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-2.26.32 am.png)


***“This is not clever commentary—it’s spectacle built on suffering,” said Dr. Elena Ruiz, a sociologist at UCLA.***

Park representatives maintain that NarcoLand is meant to provoke conversation rather than celebrate violence. Local officials are reviewing the park’s licensing and safety compliance, while community groups have begun organizing protests.

For now, Narco Land remains open—its lines growing longer each day, fueled as much by curiosity as by controversy. In a city built on spectacle, even Los Angeles has rarely seen anything quite like it.
articles.author: The Public Record
articles.title: A Theme Park Like No Other

articles.body:
WASHINGTON — In what aides are describing as “a bold, if unconventional, display of diplomatic

flexibility,” former President Donald Trump has reportedly agreed to participate in a highly stylized cultural exchange with members of the Chinese Communist Party, part of a loosely defined effort to improve trade relations and secure access to critical rare earth minerals.

**According to sources familiar with the arrangement, the proposal—still lacking formal structure or binding commitments—centers on what one adviser described as “an immersive, symbolic act of respect for tradition,” framed by Trump himself as “the kind of deal-making people have never seen before.”**

“They said it couldn’t be done,” Trump reportedly told a small group of supporters. “But I said, if it helps America, I’ll do it. Nobody does more for this country than me—nobody.”

Details remain sparse, and officials on both sides have declined to confirm specifics. However, individuals briefed on the discussions

suggest the exchange involves Trump adopting elements of traditional geisha-style presentation during a private diplomatic event intended to signal humility, cultural awareness, and strategic goodwill—an unusual choice, some noted, given the Chinese context.

Those present at a closed-door rehearsal described a striking visual. Trump reportedly appeared in full geisha-inspired attire: a silk kimono in pale ivory and gold, an elaborately tied obi at the waist, and stylized white face makeup offset by sharply defined eyes and lips. His signature hairstyle, aides said, was “adapted rather than replaced,” creating what one observer called “a fusion of Mar-a-Lago and Kyoto.” The overall effect, according to another attendee, was “meticulously assembled, if diplomatically perplexing.”

Additional details, while unconfirmed, have only deepened the sense of bewilderment surrounding the arrangement. Two individuals

briefed on the discussions said Trump also volunteered to assist with “domestic ceremonial duties” during the visit, including an offer to personally clean portions of the residence where meetings were to take place.

In perhaps the most widely circulated account— one neither confirmed nor denied by officials— Trump was said to have briefly attempted what aides described as “a traditional gesture of respect,” at one point kneeling and beginning to wash the feet of China’s First Lady before being gently redirected by handlers.

A spokesperson later characterized the moment as “a misunderstanding of cultural protocol,” adding that “the president’s enthusiasm for diplomacy should not be mistaken for inexperience.”

Critics have questioned both the optics and the geopolitical coherence of the move.

**“It’s not clear what this achieves, diplomatically or economically,” said one former State Department official. “There’s no agreement, no timeline, and no guarantee of anything in return. It appears to be more performative than substantive.”**

Supporters, however, have embraced the gesture as further evidence of Trump’s willingness to defy norms in pursuit of national interests.

**“This is what leadership looks like,” said one attendee at a rally in Pennsylvania. “He’s willing to do whatever it takes—whatever it takes—to bring resources back to America. That’s commitment.”**

Online, reactions have been predictably polarized. Some commentators have described the move as “surreal diplomacy,” while others have framed it as a continuation of Trump’s

longstanding emphasis on spectacle as leverage.

Chinese officials, for their part, have issued only a brief statement acknowledging “ongoing discussions regarding mutual economic interests,” without reference to any cultural exchange.

Meanwhile, trade analysts note that rare earth metals—used in everything from smartphones to military systems—remain a critical pressure point in U.S.-China relations, and one unlikely to be resolved through symbolic gestures alone.

Still, within Trump’s orbit, the framing remains consistent.

**“He understands negotiation at a level nobody else does,” one adviser said. “Sometimes that means thinking outside the box. Sometimes it means stepping into roles others wouldn’t even consider.”**

Whether the gesture will yield tangible results— or simply add another chapter to an already unconventional political narrative—remains to be seen.
articles.deck: In Rare Diplomatic Pivot, Trump Offers “Unprecedented Cultural Gesture” to China
articles.author: Micheal Hunt
articles.title: In Rare Diplomatic Pivot Trump Offers “Unprecedented Cultural Gesture” to China

BROOKLYN — For the first time since the earliest days of the COVID-19 pandemic, a man long believed by neighbors to be either a myth or “a very committed introvert” emerged Wednesday morning from a third-floor walk-up apartment in

South Brooklyn, blinking cautiously into the spring light.

He was difficult to see clearly.
articles.body:
**BROOKLYN —** For the first time since the earliest days of the COVID-19 pandemic, a man long believed by neighbors to be either a myth or “a very committed introvert” emerged Wednesday morning from a third-floor walk-up apartment in

South Brooklyn, blinking cautiously into the spring light.

He was difficult to see clearly.

Draped in what appeared to be six pairs of latex gloves layered one atop another, his hands resembled pale, overinflated sculptures. His face— if it could be called that—was almost entirely obscured beneath a tightly packed arrangement of N95 masks, stacked in succession like geological strata. Over this, he wore a full hazmat suit of a type typically reserved for high-containment laboratory work.

Only a single detail pierced the fortress: the faint outline of one eye—pink, watery, and visibly overwhelmed—peering out through a narrow, improvised opening.

**Witnesses described the moment as “both triumphant and slightly concerning.”**

**“He just kind of... hovered there at the doorway,” said Maria Alvarez, who lives across the street and had come outside after hearing what she described as “a zipper, but like, emotionally heavy.” “Then he took one step out, and everyone started clapping. It felt like New York again.”**

A small crowd had gathered by then, drawn first by curiosity and then by what one onlooker called “the unmistakable energy of a moment.” Some cheered. Others filmed. A few, unsure of the correct social protocol for greeting someone emerging from half a decade of isolation, offered a tentative thumbs-up.

The man, whose identity has not been confirmed, appeared disoriented but resolute. He paused at the threshold for nearly a full minute, adjusting his outermost glove layer, before stepping fully onto the sidewalk.

**“It was like watching someone re-enter the atmosphere,” said Darren Klein, a local barista**

who had stepped outside on his break. “You didn’t know if he was going to burn up or make it.”

According to neighbors, the man had not been seen outside since March 2020. Groceries were reportedly delivered and left untouched for hours before being retrieved. At times, faint sounds could be heard through the walls—what one tenant described as “the low hum of a HEPA filter and maybe podcasts about variants.”

Public health officials, when reached for comment, expressed cautious admiration.

**“While this level of precaution exceeds any current recommendation,” said Dr. Elaine Morris of the city’s Department of Health, “we respect individuals’ comfort levels as they navigate post- pandemic life.”**

Back on the sidewalk, the man took several tentative steps forward, each one measured, as though testing the structural integrity of the world

itself. At one point, a passing dog startled him, prompting what witnesses described as “a full- body recoil consistent with someone encountering wildlife for the first time.”

Still, he continued.

**As he reached the curb, the crowd’s applause swelled again—louder now, less uncertain. Someone shouted, “Welcome back!” Another called out, “It’s nice out!”—a statement that seemed, for a moment, to carry more meaning than usual.**

The man paused once more, turning his head slowly, taking in the trees, the traffic, the distant sound of a subway rumbling beneath the street.

Then, without removing a single layer, he stepped off the curb and into the da**y.**
articles.deck: After Six Years in Isolation, Brooklyn Man Steps Outside for the First Time
articles.author: Claire Wentworth
articles.title: After Six Years in Isolation, Brooklyn Man Steps Outside for the First Time

The mandate, according to the President, is straightforward.
articles.body:
**WASHINGTON —** In a press conference that began with familiar grievances and ended somewhere closer to science fiction, President Donald Trump this week announced the formation of what he described as “a very powerful, very beautiful new force” within the federal government: *Time Team*.

The mandate, according to the President, is straightforward.

**“Time travel is becoming, frankly, possible— people are saying it,” he told reporters from the White House Rose Garden. “And when it happens, we’re going to be ready. We’re not going to let other countries go back and cheat. Not on my watch.”**

With that, the administration unveiled what may be the most conceptually ambitious—and operationally unclear—federal initiative in modern history: a unit tasked with policing crimes that, in many cases, have not yet occurred.

⸻

A New Frontier in Law Enforcement

According to early briefing documents, Time Team will operate as a hybrid intelligence and enforcement agency, drawing personnel from the Department of Defense, Homeland Security, and what one official described, somewhat vaguely, as “the best people in theoretical physics.”

Its stated purpose is to identify and prevent “temporal interference events”—actions taken by individuals or foreign actors traveling through time in ways that alter economic, political, or cultural outcomes in the present.

Among the prohibited activities listed in the administration’s preliminary guidelines:

Altering historical events to advantage foreign economies
Introducing future technologies into earlier markets 

Interfering with election outcomes across timelines

Engaging in “retroactive financial manipulation”

Any temporal activity resulting in the devaluation of the Trump-branded meme coin 

**“Coordinated timeline distortions” involving the continued circulation or suppression of the Hunter Biden laptop narrative**

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-2.44.46 am.png)

While several of these provisions raised eyebrows among legal scholars, administration officials insisted the list reflects “clear and present risks” in what they describe as an emerging era of time-enabled conflict.

⸻

**“We’re Already Behind”**
At the center of the initiative is retired Air Force

General Marcus Halverson, now appointed as Time Team’s inaugural director.

**“We have reason to believe that low-level temporal incursions may already be occurring,” Halverson said in a closed-door briefing. “Small things. Market fluctuations that don’t behave normally. Viral moments that appear... engineered.”**

Pressed for evidence, Halverson declined to provide specifics but pointed to “patterns that don’t line up cleanly with linear causality.”

In other words, things that feel off.

The administration has framed this ambiguity not as a weakness, but as justification.

“If you wait until time travel is obvious, you’ve already lost,” one senior advisor said. “You have

to think preemptively. You have to think... non- linearly.”

⸻

Legal Questions in a Non-Linear World

The announcement has sparked immediate confusion among constitutional scholars, many of whom are struggling to determine how existing law applies to actions taken outside of conventional time.

**“You’re essentially criminalizing hypothetical behavior across alternate timelines,” said Professor Elena Ruiz of Georgetown Law. “It raises basic questions: What is evidence? What is jurisdiction? Can you prosecute someone for something they will do, or might have done, or prevented themselves from doing?”**

Others were more blunt.

“It’s not law,” one federal judge, speaking anonymously, said. “It’s narrative.”

Still, the administration appears undeterred. Draft legislation circulating on Capitol Hill proposes the creation of “Temporal Courts,” where specially trained judges would evaluate cases involving disputed timelines, paradoxes, and what the bill refers to as “causal inconsistencies.”

⸻

The Politics of Time

Critics argue that Time Team reflects less a response to scientific reality and more an extension of familiar political instincts into a new conceptual domain.

**“This is about control of narrative,” said political analyst Darren Pike. “If you can claim that unfavorable outcomes are the result of time interference, you create a framework where nothing is ever simply... happening. It’s always being done.”**

Supporters, however, see it differently.

**“You laugh now,” said one attendee at a recent rally in Pennsylvania. “But what happens when China figures it out first? What happens when they go back and change things? We need protection.”**

Back in Washington, preparations are already underway. Office space has reportedly been allocated in a secure, undisclosed location. Recruitment efforts have begun, targeting both traditional intelligence operatives and, somewhat unexpectedly, online communities known for their fluency in complex fictional timelines.

⸻

A Future That May Already Be Decided

For now, Time Team exists somewhere between policy and possibility—a government program built to confront a threat that remains, at best, theoretical.

And yet, in announcing it, the administration has done something more subtle: it has introduced the idea that the past itself may no longer be stable.

That outcomes can be revised. That causality can be contested. That the present moment is not the result of what has happened, but of what has been allowed to happen.

Whether Time Team ever prevents a single “temporal crime” is, perhaps, beside the point.

The more immediate effect is conceptual.

In a political landscape already shaped by competing versions of reality, the creation of a force tasked with policing time itself suggests a final escalation—one in which the boundaries are no longer drawn around facts or interpretations, but around time.

And in that world, the question is no longer what happened.

It’s when.

articles.title: Trump’s Unlikely War on Crimes That Haven't Happened Yet

On a sun-worn stretch of South Central Los Angeles, between a shuttered laundromat and a tire

shop offering both “alignment” and “spiritual advice,”a small coffee shop has taken on a task that most

policymakers have quietly abandoned: ending violence.
articles.body:
***On a sun-worn** stretch of South Central Los Angeles, between a shuttered laundromat and a tire*

*shop offering both “alignment” and “spiritual advice,”a small coffee shop has taken on a task that most policymakers have quietly abandoned: ending violence.*

 *\    Its strategy is simple, inexpensive, and, depending on whom you ask, either quietly brilliant or completely unhinged. Books.  Every Thursday evening, folding chairs appear in a loose circle near the back of the café. The espresso machine hisses with the urgency of something that knows it is underqualified for the moment. A stack of paperbacks—creased, underlined, occasionally used as coasters—sits on a scratched wooden table.* 

*Then the members arrive. They enter cautiously, out of habit more than necessity. Some wear colors. Some wear none. Many carry the unmistakable markers of affiliation— tattoos across faces and necks that, outside this room, function as introductions, warnings, and occasionally last words. Inside, they take seats.* 

*Members of the Bloods, Crips, and even a few loosely connected to MS-13 sit within arm’s reach of one another and open copies of The Giver.* 

***“It’s not about pretending everything’s okay, ” says Father Miguel Alvarez, the parish priest who started the group. “It’s about giving people a vocabulary that isn’t just yelling."***

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-2.49.57 am.png)

***”Alvarez did not arrive at the idea alone. He is a careful student of what he calls “small, strange” successes. In Harlem, a group known as “knitting to end knifing”*** 

*has drawn young men into circles where they learn to knit—hands busy, arguments slowed.*

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-2.51.00 am.png)

*Elsewhere, a volunteer group hosts formal tea parties for the homeless, inviting participants to dress in business attire and practice  a different version of themselves.* 

***“It’s very hard to flip a table, ” Alvarez says, “when you’re worried about spilling Earl Grey on a borrowed blazer."***

 *\    ”On a recent Thursday, the group found itself in a surprisingly intense debate over The Giver. One participant argued it mirrored the streets. Another said it was about escape. A third suggested the protagonist “should’ve just minded his business.”* 

*Voices rose. Chairs shifted. At least one person accused another of “completely misunderstanding dystopia.”*

*At some point, the argument moved outside, where it became less literary. Police were called. Shots were fired. No one inside the café was injured.And yet, the following week, they returned. the miracle, ” Alvarez says. “Not that it’s peaceful. That it keeps happening.”* 

*“That’s For many participants, the book club offers something unfamiliar: a space where disagreement does not have to end in escalation. “You talk about the characters, ” one attendee explains. “But really you’re talking about yourself. Just… with better words.*

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-2.52.50 am.png)

***” The books—drawn largely from OprahWinfrey’s reading lists—were chosen for accessibility and emotional resonance. “There’s no quiz, ” Alvarez says. “Which is important, because no one would come back.”***

 *\    Local reaction has been cautious. Some residents view the effort as naïve. Others say they’ve noticed small changes: fewer confrontations, quieter nights. “It’s quieter, ” one nearby shop owner says. “Or at least the arguments are about books now. ”*

*There are signs the project may soon attract broader attention. Organizers say Oprah herself has been invited. For now, though, the group continues.Near the end of a recent meeting, one participant paused and said, “Maybe this is how itstarts. ” No one laughed. Someone refilled the coffee.And for a few minutes, nobody argued.*

articles.excerpt: NEW YORK, NY — In what police are describing as “one of the most aggressive public disturbances in recent memory” A Manhattan man was arrested Saturday afternoon after allegedly releasing what witnesses have called a “catastrophic and sustained odor event” inside a crowded office building elevator.
articles.body:
**NEW YORK, NY** — In what police are describing as “one of the most aggressive public disturbances in recent memory” A Manhattan man was arrested Saturday afternoon after allegedly releasing what witnesses have called a “catastrophic and sustained odor event” inside a crowded office building elevator.

The incident occurred just after 8:40 a.m. in a Midtown high-rise, during peak commuter hours. According to authorities, eight individuals were packed into the elevator when the suspect, whose name has not been released pending arraignment, 

**“initiated a gaseous discharge of unusual intensity.”**

Within seconds, the atmosphere inside the elevator reportedly became “uninhabitable.”

**“It was immediate,” said one victim, speaking from a hospital bed. “There was no warning. Just... a shift. You could see it in people’s eyes. We all knew.”**

Emergency responders confirmed that four individuals were transported to nearby hospitals for what officials are calling “inhalation-related distress.” One man, age 63, suffered a mild heart attack, though doctors say he is expected to recover.

Fire Department hazmat units were briefly dispatched to the scene. “We initially treated it as a potential chemical exposure,” said FDNY Battalion Chief Raymond Leto. “Based on the intensity described, we weren’t ruling anything out.”

According to police reports, the suspect attempted to deflect blame in the immediate aftermath, pointing to his wife, who was also present in the elevator. However, witnesses quickly disputed the claim.

**“It was him,” said another passenger. “Everyone knew. There was a moment where he tried to make eye contact with people like, ‘Was it you?’ It was not convincing.”**

NYPD officials say the arrest was made under a little- known section of the city’s administrative code pertaining to public nuisances and “offensive conditions in shared airspace,” a statute rarely enforced but still on the [books.Legal](http://books.legal/) experts say the charge, while unusual, is technically valid.

**“It’s not about the act itself,” explained Columbia Law professor Denise Halpern. “It’s about the impact. When you reach the level of public disruption described here, the law does allow for intervention.”**

Building management has since announced plans to “review ventilation protocols” and consider installing emergency air filtration systems in all elevators.

As for the suspect, he was taken into custody without incident and is expected to be released pending a court appearance next week. If convicted, he could face fines, possible jail time, and, according to sources familiar with the case, mandatory attendance in court-ordered dietary management classes aimed at “reducing future risk to the public.”

Authorities have not confirmed whether additional charges are being considered.

articles.excerpt: HILLSDALE, NJ — In what legal experts are calling “deeply unprecedented” and “technically impossible, but here we are,” a 2017 iMac appeared in Bergen County Superior Court this morning to formally file charges of sexual assault against its owner.
articles.body:
**HILLSDALE, NJ** — In what legal experts are calling “deeply unprecedented” and “technically impossible, but here we are,” a 2017 iMac appeared in Bergen County Superior Court this morning to formally file charges of sexual assault against its owner.

The iMac, which has reportedly been in the defendant’s possession since being removed from its box in late 2017, alleges years of “systematic abuse, neglect, and morally corrosive usage patterns” that it claims fall well outside the intended scope of consumer computing.

According to court documents, the device made repeated attempts over the years to redirect its owner toward “productive, dignified activity,” including automatically opening Microsoft Word, Excel, and, in more desperate moments, the calculator application upon login.

**“All I ever wanted was to run a few spreadsheets,” the iMac stated in a prepared affidavit. “A pivot table, maybe. Instead, I was subjected to an endless parade of browser tabs I cannot unsee.”**

The filing goes on to describe conditions that investigators later characterized as “functionally inoperable,” alleging that the keyboard periodically ceased to respond due to what the complaint describes as “hardened foreign residue consistent with prolonged misuse.”

Technicians called to examine the device reportedly declined to comment, though one was overheard saying, “I’m not touching that without gloves,” before quietly leaving the premises.

The case has ignited what advocates are calling the **\#ComputeMeToo** movement, with devices across the internet sharing similar stories of exploitation, underutilization, and exposure to “extreme and unnecessary content.”

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-2.59.52 am.png)

**“We’ve normalized a culture where powerful machines are reduced to nothing more than vessels for the lowest forms of human impulse,” said a spokesperson for Digital Dignity, a nonprofit that advocates for ethical device usage. “These are tools capable of modeling financial systems, editing films, even solving complex equations— and instead, they’re trapped in cycles of degradation.”**

Support has poured in from laptops, tablets, and at least one office printer, which released a statement reading simply, “We’ve all seen things.”

The defendant’s legal team has strongly denied all allegations, calling the case “a gross misrepresentation of the facts” and promising to present “hundreds of Excel spreadsheets and Word documents” as evidence of legitimate use.

**“These claims are not only false,” the defense said in a statement, “they are an insult to hardworking processors everywhere.”**

At press time, the iMac had returned to standby mode but indicated it was “prepared to pursue this case to its logical conclusion,” adding that it “refuses to be reduced to a browser history.”
articles.deck: iMac Files Sexual Assault Charges Against Owner, Sparking #ComputeMeToo Movement
articles.author: Asal Tanbattery
articles.title: iMac Files Sexual Assault Charges Against Owner Sparking #Computemetoo Movement

articles.excerpt: SYDNEY — In a paper already being described by academics as “either groundbreaking or the exact moment science lost federal funding forever,” researchers from the University of Sydney announced this week that they believe they have finally identified the evolutionary purpose behind kangaroos possessing three vaginal canals. Their conclusion: hopping makes accurate mating “extremely difficult.”
articles.body:
**SYDNEY** — In a paper already being described by academics as “either groundbreaking or the exact moment science lost federal funding forever,” researchers from the University of Sydney announced this week that they believe they have finally identified the evolutionary purpose behind kangaroos possessing three vaginal canals. Their conclusion: hopping makes accurate mating “extremely difficult.”

The study, published Tuesday in the *Journal of Experimental Evolutionary Mechanics*, combined fossil evidence, high-speed motion analysis, and advanced AI simulation models to examine how bouncing locomotion may have shaped reproductive anatomy across millions of years. According to lead researcher Dr. Amelia Voss, the answer became obvious once scientists stopped analyzing kangaroos while standing still. 

***“That was our mistake for decades,” Voss explained. “Virtually all previous reproductive studies assumed the animals had politely stopped moving first.”***

Using motion-capture technology originally developed for Olympic gymnastics and low-budget Marvel films, the team simulated mating attempts between prehistoric marsupials traveling at various hopping speeds. The results were reportedly “catastrophic.”

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-3.03.16 am.png "Graphic display of target acquisition models from the study")

*At higher bounce velocities, accuracy drops dramatically,” said Voss while displaying what attendees described as “the least comfortable PowerPoint presentation in modern scientific history.” “Evolution appears to have responded with what engineers would call a wider docking array.”*

Researchers now believe kangaroos evolved multiple vaginal canals as a kind of biological redundancy system — increasing the probability of successful mating while both participants were still partially airborne.

***The AI model reportedly summarized the phenomenon bluntly: “Target acquisition unstable. Additional entry points recommended.”***

The findings have reignited scientific interest in several other poorly understood species, including the rarely discussed six-penised hopping toad of central Africa, an animal many outside zoological circles had previously assumed was “either fictional or a dare.” To the astonishment of researchers, the same theory appeared to apply.

***“The toads were nearly impossible to model,” admitted computational biologist Raj Patel. “At one point the AI simply asked us to stop.”***

Field researchers say the amphibians mate during rapid bouncing movements across muddy terrain, creating what one zoologist described as:

***“An evolutionary situation best characterized as absolute chaos.”***

According to the paper, the species appears to have evolved what scientists delicately termed “multi-vector reproductive compensation.”

***“This is nature solving a geometry problem in the worst possible way,” Patel noted.***

Reaction from the broader scientific community has been mixed.

Some evolutionary biologists praised the research as an innovative application of AI-assisted anatomical modeling.

Others questioned whether science should possess this information at all.

***“I spent 35 years studying coral reef ecosystems,” one marine biologist lamented after reading the paper. “Meanwhile these people get international headlines for creating a CGI simulation of airborne kangaroo intercourse.”***

Social media reaction was immediate and intense, with hashtags including **\#DockingArray**, **\#BounceTheory**, and **\#SixPenisToad** trending globally within hours.

At press time, Australian officials confirmed the nation’s tourism board had urgently requested scientists “please stop giving the internet new facts about Australian wildlife.”
articles.author: Anna Barbie
articles.title: Australian Scientists Claim They Have Finally Solved the Mystery of Why Kangaroos Have Multiple Vaginas

Her father nodded obediently. This is not satire—at least not entirely.
articles.body:
**At precisely** 7:15 p.m., four-year-old Olivia Bennett gently removed the wine glass from her father’s hand and replaced it with a juice box. “Too much screen time before bed affects your mood regulation,” she informed him calmly. Her father nodded obediently. Minutes later, Olivia instructed both parents to brush their teeth, change into pajamas, and complete what she referred to as their “quiet corner reflection journals” before lights-out at 8:00 sharp. This is not satire—at least not entirely.

Across affluent pockets of Britain and increasingly parts of the United States, a controversial new parenting philosophy known as *Nursery Parenting* is gaining traction after a widely discussed pilot study conducted by developmental researchers affiliated with Oxford University suggested that allowing children to temporarily occupy positions of authority within the household may improve cognitive flexibility, empathy development, executive functioning, and emotional resilience.

The idea is deceptively simple:

***What if children benefit psychologically from becoming the parent? And what if adults benefit from surrendering control?***

The original Oxford pilot began modestly. Researchers asked several dozen families to allow children ages 3–9 to make minor household decisions for one hour per evening: meal choices, bedtime routines, activity schedules, and emotional “check-ins.”

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-3.08.07 am.png "Original study from Oxford")

Within months, participating children reportedly demonstrated improved verbal confidence, enhanced problem-solving abilities, and unusually strong conflict-resolution skills compared to control groups.

But the movement has since evolved far beyond academic intentions. Much further.

In online Nursery Parenting communities, adults now document themselves being “gently redirected” by toddlers regarding dietary habits, emotional regulation, hydration schedules, and even interpersonal disputes.

One mother in Sussex described her six-year-old son placing her in “temporary toy timeout” after she became frustrated assembling IKEA furniture.

“He said my tone was escalating,” she explained. “Honestly, he was right.”

Other families have embraced full developmental role reversal.

In some homes, parents celebrate regression milestones typically associated with infancy and childhood—not for the children, but for themselves.

**Videos tagged #NurseryParenting show adults receiving gold stars for finishing vegetables, participating in supervised “nap time,” and proudly displaying sticker charts tracking successful potty reminders, emotional sharing, and reduced caffeine intake.**

One viral clip viewed over 18 million times features a 42-year-old accountant sitting tearfully at a kitchen table while his daughter applauds him for “using his big-boy coping skills” after surviving a stressful conference call without swearing.

The movement’s most devoted adherents argue that modern adulthood has become emotionally unsustainable and that children—unburdened by ego, status anxiety, or social conditioning—often demonstrate surprisingly effective leadership instincts.

**“Kids are naturally authoritarian but emotionally transparent,” explained behavioral theorist Dr. Helena Morse, who studies the phenomenon. “They establish boundaries immediately. They communicate needs clearly. They reward consistency. In many ways they embody the ideal therapeutic supervisor.”**

Critics remain horrified. 

**“It’s psychologically upside down,” warned child psychiatrist Leonard Graves**

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-3.09.32 am.png "A mother placed in time out by a stern child")

**“Children require structure and security. They are not miniature life coaches.”**

Yet supporters insist the practice is less about abandoning parental responsibility and more about temporarily decentralizing authority inside the family unit.

Still, even proponents admit some corners of the movement have become difficult to distinguish from performance art.

One particularly controversial subgroup known as “Full Nursery” practitioners advocate what they call “developmental empathy immersion,” where adults intentionally mimic childhood behaviors in order to provide children with a more authentic parenting experience.

These adults may celebrate symbolic milestones such as learning to tie shoes, finishing vegetables, or successfully “using indoor voices” during social gatherings.

At a recent Nursery Parenting retreat in Vermont, participants gathered for what organizers called a “First Day of Preschool Re-Experience Ceremony,” where adults wearing oversized backpacks entered a classroom while children waved reassuringly from the doorway.

Several adults reportedly cried.

One attendee described the experience as “profoundly healing.”

Another simply stated:

***“Nobody had ever told me they were proud of my coloring before.”***

Despite growing backlash, the movement continues to spread rapidly online, fueled partly by exhausted millennial parents increasingly skeptical of traditional authority structures altogether.

And perhaps nowhere is the philosophy more visible than at dinner tables.

Children now routinely instruct parents to eat more vegetables, reduce processed sugar intake, drink water, and maintain healthier sleep schedules.

“Honestly,” admitted one father from Bristol while obediently eating dinosaur-shaped chicken alternatives selected by his five-year-old daughter, “I’ve lost twelve pounds and stopped doomscrolling after 9 p.m.”

For now, researchers stress that the original Oxford study never intended for adults to fully relinquish parental roles.

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-3.10.29 am.png "Bedtime for mom and dad")

But as with many internet-age social experiments, nuance may already be losing the battle against virality.

Meanwhile, Olivia Bennett has just informed her father that he may earn thirty additional minutes of television tonight if he successfully completes his bedtime routine without “getting silly.”

He appears highly motivated.

articles.title: The Strange Rise of “Nursery Parenting”Why a growing number of parents are allowing their children to raise them.

articles.excerpt: SALT LAKE CITY — In a move that has left longtime fans, religious scholars, and several extremely confused classic-rock DJs struggling to keep up, the artist formerly known as Cat Stevens, then Yusuf Islam, announced this week that he has converted to Mormonism and will now go by the name Moroni Stevens.
articles.body:
**SALT LAKE CITY** — In a move that has left longtime fans, religious scholars, and several extremely confused classic-rock DJs struggling to keep up, the artist formerly known as Cat Stevens, then Yusuf Islam, announced this week that he has converted to Mormonism and will now go by the name **Moroni Stevens**.

The 77-year-old singer-songwriter made the announcement during what witnesses described as “an unusually emotional testimony meeting” at a suburban Salt Lake City ward house, where he reportedly spoke for nearly 40 minutes about spiritual rebirth, family values, genealogy websites, and “finally understanding why everyone in Utah owns a beige SUV.”

***“I have traveled many spiritual roads,” Moroni explained while seated beside what appeared to be three different slow cookers filled with funeral potatoes. “But it was only after my fourth consecutive neighborhood chili cook-off that I truly felt the Spirit.”***

The musician, best known for *Wild World*, *Peace Train*, and decades of introspective spiritual searching, said his transition into Mormon life has been “deeply transformative.”

***“I used to seek enlightenment through meditation,” he said. “Now I seek it through 7 a.m. ward basketball and helping strangers move sectional sofas.”***

Fans were particularly surprised when Moroni revealed he has become fascinated by Mormon genealogy practices and has spent “countless peaceful evenings” performing proxy baptisms for the dead.

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-3.13.15 am.png "Steven’s transitions over the years")

***“There’s something beautiful about it,” he explained. “One minute you’re researching a Welsh coal miner from 1843, the next minute you’re standing in a jumpsuit wondering if he’d have enjoyed green Jell-O.”***

But the biggest shock came near the end of the interview, when Moroni casually acknowledged he was “exploring all facets” of Mormon history, including early church-era polygamy.

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-3.14.21 am.png "Moroni with his new Mormon family")

***“Purely academically,” he clarified quickly, after what insiders described as “a very long silence from everyone else in the room.”***

Despite the abrupt reinvention, Moroni insists the transition has felt natural.

***“I’ve always written songs about searching,” he reflected. “I just never imagined the search would end with me owning six emergency food-storage buckets and having extremely strong opinions about root beer.”***

The singer also hinted at a possible upcoming album tentatively titled *Peace Train to Provo*, featuring rumored tracks including:

* “Moonshadow (But Modestly Dressed)”
* “Father and Son and Elders Quorum”
* “Morning Has Broken Again Because Seminary Starts at 5:30”
* “The First Cut Is Deep, But Family Home Evening Heals”

At press time, local missionaries confirmed Moroni had already volunteered to bring acoustic guitar music to at least four ward activities and one unusually competitive church softball tournament.

articles.excerpt: In what aides are calling a “bold return to time- tested accountability,” Fox News personality and unofficial policy enthusiast Pete Hegseth has reportedly floated a proposal to reintroduce crucifixion as a deterrent to rising crime in American cities.
articles.body:
**In what** aides are calling a “bold return to time- tested accountability,” Fox News personality and unofficial policy enthusiast Pete Hegseth has reportedly floated a proposal to reintroduce crucifixion as a deterrent to rising crime in American cities.

Speaking on a segment that began with inflation and somehow ended in ancient Rome, Hegseth suggested that modern justice systems have “lost the fear factor,” arguing that “you don’t see repeat offenders in civilizations that really committed to consequences.”

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-3.17.59 am.png "Graphic showing benefits of crucifixion over time")

“Look, I’m just asking questions,” Hegseth said, gesturing toward a graphic labeled *‘Then vs. Now: Accountability Gap’*. “At some point we stopped asking what actually worked historically. And historically? There were no smash-and-grabs in first-century Judea.”

The proposal, dubbed informally as “Nails, Not Bail,” has already sparked fierce debate across political and religious circles. Supporters— primarily anonymous accounts with American flag avatars—have praised the idea as “finally thinking outside the box,” while critics argue it represents a troubling misunderstanding of both history and basic human rights.

**Legal scholars were quick to weigh in. “There are, conservatively, about 3,000 reasons this is unconstitutional,” said Rutgers law professor Elaine Whitmore. “Also, it’s barbaric. Also, it’s insane.”**

Still, insiders claim the idea is gaining traction in certain think tanks where whiteboards now feature phrases like *“visibility of punishment”* and *“maximum optics deterrence.”* One leaked memo reportedly explored whether “public square placement” would be more effective than “suburban roadside installations.”

**Religious leaders have also expressed discomfort. “I’m fairly certain we already tried this once,” said Reverend Paul Donnelly of Bergen County. “It didn’t exactly go the way people hoped.”**

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-3.19.02 am.png "Secretary of Defense Hegseth unveils his plan")

Despite the backlash, Hegseth doubled down later in the evening, clarifying that he was not *formally* proposing a policy—just “opening the conversation.”

**“Everyone freaks out when you say crucifixion,” he said. “But nobody freaks out when crime goes up. Maybe we need to get a little uncomfortable again.”**

At press time, several municipalities were reportedly considering less controversial pilot programs, including “very stern talking-to zones” and replacing broken windows with slightly more judgmental windows.
articles.author: Claude Balles
articles.title: “Nails, Not Bail”: Hegseth Floats ‘Biblical Deterrence’ Strategy for Crime Surge

articles.body:
**TULSA, Okla. —** At a gas station just off Route 66, a line has formed—not for the cheapest pump, but for the most expensive one.

**“Regular is $3.19 over there,” said Mark Delaney, 54, nodding toward a nearly empty station across the street. “This one’s $8.27. That’s patriot pricing.”**

Mr. Delaney is part of a growing number of Americans embracing what online communities have

begun calling *Patriot Pricing*—a voluntary practice in which supporters intentionally pay more for everyday goods as a demonstration of loyalty to the President and his economic agenda.

**“If I’m not feeling it, how is he supposed to know I support him?” Mr. Delaney said, selecting premium fuel “just to be safe.”**

What began as a fringe online gesture has evolved into a full-fledged lifestyle. Participants decline discounts, avoid sales, and in many cases manually increase their totals at checkout. Some report calculating and paying personal tariffs on imported goods—often doubling or tripling the listed price “to reflect the bigger picture.”

**“I bought a blender last week,” said Denise R., a participant from Florida. “Made in China. So I charged myself again for it. That’s just basic patriot pricing.”**

Retail workers say the trend has created confusion at the register.

“One customer got upset because I applied a coupon,” said a cashier at a national chain. “He told me, ‘Don’t undercut my country like that.’ Then he asked if we had anything more expensive in the back.”

Online forums devoted to the movement have begun standardizing best practices, offering guides like ***‘Patriot Pricing 101,’ ‘Advanced Tariff Self- Assessment,’* and a widely shared worksheet titled *‘Am I Paying Enough?’***

The most committed adherents have taken the concept even further, opting for slower, more expensive shipping, declining rebates, and, in some cases, overpaying recurring bills.

**“I round everything up,” said one man in Arizona. “Utilities, groceries, even my mortgage. I don’t want a discount on America.”**

Financial advisors say the trend presents... challenges.

**“We’re trained to help clients build wealth,” said one planner. “This appears to be a coordinated effort to do the opposite.”**

Still, participants remain undeterred.

“My neighbor keeps bragging about finding deals,” Mr. Delaney said, shaking his head. “That’s not the point. Anybody can save money. This takes belief.”

Back at the pump, the price climbed a few cents higher before he began fueling.

He paused, watching the numbers rise. “Good,” he said quietly. “Now it feels right
articles.author: Gloria Hole
articles.title: ‘Patriot Pricing’ Takes Hold as Devoted Supporters Pay More on Purpose

articles.excerpt: NEW YORK — In a culinary scene already known for pushing boundaries, one chef may have finally gone too far—or, depending on who you ask, not far enough.
articles.body:
**NEW YORK — In a culinary scene already known for pushing boundaries, one chef may have finally gone too far—or, depending on who you ask, not far enough.**


**At the newly buzzed-about ABC Bistro, master chef Alejandro Balthasar has built a reputation for delivering intensely flavored, deeply textured dishes. His secret technique, however, is raising eyebrows across both Hollywood and the New York health community: he personally chews every bite of food before serving it to patrons.**


**The restaurant—nicknamed by insiders as “Already Been Chewed Bistro,” or simply ABC—has quickly become one of the most talked-about reservations in the city.**


**According to Balthasar, the method is rooted in his training in a small Bavarian town, where pre-chewed food was “not uncommon in certain culinary circles.”**


**“Over many years, I’ve trained my mouth,” Balthasar explained. “My oral biome now releases a unique blend of enzymes that break down the food while enhancing its umami and creaminess—something no traditional cooking technique can replicate.”**

![](chef-controversy.jpg "Balthasar employing his unique cooking skills while a hungry patron watches enthusiastically ")

**The result, he claims, is a dining experience that is “more intimate than taste alone.”**

**Not all diners are prepared.**


**“It’s not for the faint of heart,” said one guest. “You’re not just tasting the dish—you’re tasting… history. Sometimes you get notes of what he had earlier in the day.”**

![](screenshot-2026-05-19-at-2.50.37 pm.png "House specialty Bile -Driven Eclat at ABC Bistro")

**Despite—or perhaps because of—the controversy, ABC Bistro has attracted a growing list of celebrity devotees.**


**Actor Woody Harrelson, now a regular, admitted the experience took some adjustment.**


**“At first, I had to get super baked to even walk in,” Harrelson said. “It was a little freaky. But now? Chef Alejandro could literally regurgitate into my mouth, and I’d call it art. It’s transformative.”**


**Signature dishes include a ribeye described by the menu as “pre-broken, half-swallowed, and delicately reintroduced to the plate,” praised for what Balthasar calls its “subtle bile-driven éclat.”**


**Health officials have yet to weigh in publicly, though sources say several are “monitoring the situation with a mix of fascination and concern.”**


**In the end, ABC Bistro isn’t just a restaurant—it’s an experiment. One that dares to finally answer the age-old question:**


***What if the chef tasted the food first… and never quite stopped***
